label: Grandparent scam
blurb: A caller claiming to be a grandson, escalating to a wire transfer.

segments.text: Grandma? Hi, it's me. Your grandson. Can you hear me okay? Sorry, I know it's early.
Listen, I'm in some trouble. I was in a car accident last night, and the other driver is pressing charges. I'm at the police station right now.
Please don't tell Mom and Dad. I'm so embarrassed about this. Promise me you won't call them. Promise me, okay?
My lawyer says if we post bond today they'll release me this afternoon. It's eight thousand dollars. I know it's a lot of money.
He says the fastest way is a wire transfer. I'm going to put him on and he'll give you the account number. Please, grandma, I need you to do this right now.
No, don't hang up. Don't call anybody. If you hang up they're going to move me to the county jail tonight. Please just stay on the line with me.

label: Doctor's office (legitimate)
blurb: A real appointment reminder. The detector should stay quiet.

segments.text: Good morning, this is Maria calling from Doctor Alvarez's office at Stanford Health Care.

I'm just calling to remind you about your cardiology follow-up this Thursday at two fifteen. If you need to reschedule, give us a call back at the main number. And the doctor asked me to remind you to bring your current medication list. Thanks, see you Thursday.
